Schema Validation with Zod

Describing a shape once with z.object(...), then asking Zod whether some data matches it.

Zod lets you build a schema — an object describing what valid data looks like — out of small composable pieces, then check real data against it:

import { z } from 'zod';

const signupSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  age: z.number().int().min(13),
  newsletter: z.boolean().optional(),
});

const result = signupSchema.safeParse({ email: 'not-an-email', age: 9 });
// result.success === false
// result.error.issues → what failed, and why, for each field

z.object({...}) describes an object's shape field by field: z.string(), z.number(), z.boolean() name the type; chained calls like .email(), .int(), .min(13) add rules on top; .optional() says a field doesn't have to be present at all. None of this runs any check yet — a schema is just a description, built once, that can be reused against as many requests as the app receives.

.safeParse(data) is what actually checks data against the schema. It never throws — instead it returns { success: true, data } (with data now validated, and, as the next slide covers, coerced) or { success: false, error }, where error.issues is a detailed, field-by-field list of what was wrong. That's exactly the shape a validation middleware needs: check once, and either continue with clean data or hand back a precise list of problems — never a single vague "something's wrong" message.

(Zod also has a .parse() that throws on failure instead — not used in this project, since a thrown validation error would need its own try/catch exactly where safeParse's return value doesn't.)
